g-05b0a9c552.how: Both projects ask a similar question about complete pathways with no fitness effect, but they count different sets of organism-pathway pairs, so the shares come from different scopes.
g-05b0a9c552.question: How many complete pathways show no fitness effect under tested conditions?
g-05b0a9c552.sentence: Two projects each found genomically complete pathways whose genes showed no fitness effect under tested conditions, at 15.8% of 1,695 pathway-organism pairs in one and 41.0% (66/161) of classified pairs in the other.
g-05b0a9c552.title: Complete pathways without fitness effects, at different shares in two projects

g-1fc4cbd0a2.how: Two results report moderate concordance in the same direction but use different summary measures: percent of genes concordant versus kappa and F1. The third builds on that comparison and looks only at Complex I flux on aromatic substrates.

lanes.acinetobacter_adp1_explorer--6f19fce6: Genes with concordant FBA and TnSeq calls
lanes.adp1_triple_essentiality--d1af4698: FBA versus knockouts, kappa and F1
lanes.aromatic_catabolism_network--7d6bd2aa: Predicted Complex I flux and essentiality

g-1fc4cbd0a2.question: How well do FBA predictions match ADP1 knockout essentiality?
g-1fc4cbd0a2.sentence: Projects comparing model-predicted and knockout-based essentiality in Acinetobacter baylyi ADP1 report moderate concordance, with 639 of 866 genes concordant. The model predicts higher Complex I flux on aromatic substrates but 0% Complex I essentiality.
g-1fc4cbd0a2.title: Growth-model predictions partly match ADP1 knockout essentiality, but miss Complex I

g-2f7d211ff0.how: The comparisons are similar but differ in scope: one uses the fraction of clinical genomes in 823 species, the other uses embedding-based environmental diversity in 2,684 species. They report separate analyses and do not share data.

lanes.amr_environmental_resistome--8ab4f4eb: Clinical genome fraction versus resistance clusters
lanes.amr_pangenome_atlas--ccd6e57f: Embedding-based environmental diversity versus resistance count

g-2f7d211ff0.question: Does a species' environment predict how many resistance gene clusters it carries?
g-2f7d211ff0.sentence: Two projects linked a species' environments to its resistance gene cluster count, using clinical genome share in one and embedding-based environmental diversity in the other. Both found species with more clinical or varied environments carry more clusters.
g-2f7d211ff0.title: Environmental measures track resistance gene cluster counts per species

g-4c9467551e.how: Both compare metal resistance across environments but on different measures and scopes: one uses the share of AMR genes, the other the prevalence of metal resistance in MAGs. They do not share an analysis or data.

lanes.amr_environmental_resistome--989ebe6d: Metal share of AMR by environment
lanes.metal_resistance_global_biogeography--69: Metal resistance prevalence in MAGs by environment

g-4c9467551e.question: How does metal resistance differ across environments?
g-4c9467551e.sentence: One project found metal resistance makes up 45% of AMR in aquatic and 44% in soil but 6% in human gut. The other found soil MAGs enriched for metal resistance (5.8% prevalence), while marine MAGs were depleted (1.2%).
g-4c9467551e.title: Metal resistance is common in soil, measured by different metrics

g-5406c445fa.how: The respiratory chain project extends the aromatic network project's Complex I finding by adding NADH yield per carbon on quinate, glucose and acetate to Complex I's quinate role.

lanes.aromatic_catabolism_network--09feb273: Complex I share of quinate-specific genes
lanes.respiratory_chain_wiring--4e28db67: NADH per carbon on quinate, glucose, acetate

g-5406c445fa.question: Why does ADP1 need Complex I so strongly for aromatic catabolism?
g-5406c445fa.sentence: In Acinetobacter baylyi ADP1, Complex I accounts for 21 of 51 quinate-specific genes (41%), and quinate gives fewer NADH per carbon atom (0.57) than glucose or acetate (1.50 each), yet Complex I is more essential on quinate.
g-5406c445fa.title: Complex I dominates ADP1 quinate support despite low NADH yield

g-aff7133f14.how: Both reports give the same count of 28,017 costly but conserved genes and cite it as their strongest evidence for purifying selection. The figure is identical in the two reports, and each draws the same interpretation from it.

lanes.core_gene_tradeoffs--35113c1c: Costly core genes kept despite metabolic cost

g-aff7133f14.question: Which lab-costly genes are conserved in the pangenome, and what does that suggest?
g-aff7133f14.sentence: Two projects each report 28,017 genes that are costly in the lab yet conserved across the pangenome, and each presents them as its strongest evidence that natural environments keep these genes under purifying selection.
g-aff7133f14.title: Same 28,017 costly but conserved genes cited for purifying selection

g-b1306a0696.how: The metal specificity project extends the atlas work. It takes the atlas's 149 candidate families as its data, so both share that set, and compares their dominant specificity category with annotated families.

lanes.metal_fitness_atlas--c4506651: Finding candidate families with conserved metal fitness
lanes.metal_specificity--09020647: Metal-specific category share, candidates versus annotated

g-b1306a0696.question: How metal-specific are candidate metal families lacking full annotation compared with annotated families?
g-b1306a0696.sentence: One project found 149 candidate gene families with conserved metal fitness effects across at least two organisms but lacking full functional annotation. A second project, using those same 149 families, found 45.6% have a dominant specificity category of metal-specific, versus 58.2% of annotated families.
g-b1306a0696.title: Metal gene candidates lacking full annotation are less metal-specific than annotated families

g-b72d4df084.how: The truly-dark project extends the concordance work by asking how many of the dark-gene groups with concordance data hold truly dark genes, which was 3 of 65. Each analysis concerns 65 groups, and the results do not establish that these are the same set.

lanes.functional_dark_matter--b28eec02: Concordance of dark versus annotated ortholog groups
lanes.truly_dark_genes--682ae84a: Truly dark genes among dark ortholog groups

g-b72d4df084.question: How visible are dark genes to cross-organism concordance analysis?
g-b72d4df084.sentence: One project found that 65 dark ortholog groups showed cross-organism concordance indistinguishable from 490 annotated groups. The other found that only 3 of 65 dark-gene ortholog groups with concordance data contain truly dark genes, so those are nearly invisible to cross-organism analysis.
g-b72d4df084.title: Dark genes match annotated genes in concordance, yet few are truly dark

g-baf231a3d9.how: The pan-bacterial project extends the environmental resistome project. It adds how conserved clinical resistance genes are, building on clinical species carrying more resistance clusters.

lanes.amr_environmental_resistome--3d24fba7: Resistance cluster counts per species by source
lanes.amr_pangenome_atlas--b13c108a: Core fraction of resistance genes by environment

g-baf231a3d9.question: How do antibiotic resistance genes differ between clinical and environmental bacteria?
g-baf231a3d9.sentence: Clinical species had a median of 5 AMR gene clusters versus 2 for soil, aquatic and host-associated species. Clinical AMR was also less core (30.8%) than soil AMR (58.1%) or plant AMR (63.1%).
g-baf231a3d9.title: Clinical species carry more resistance genes, and fewer of them are core

g-ec1f436120.how: The module conservation project extends the fitness modules project by testing conservation across the cross-organism families it identified. The synthesis and module conservation projects report the same lack of link, likely because they use shared data, though this is not established.

lanes.module_conservation--3c784bf6: Conservation as gene versus module property

g-ec1f436120.question: Do module families found in more organisms have higher core fractions?
g-ec1f436120.sentence: Projects found that module families spanning more bacteria are not more often core genes, with the same correlation of -0.01 reported twice, likely from shared data. This suggests conservation is tied to individual genes rather than to how widely a module occurs.
g-ec1f436120.title: Module family breadth does not track gene conservation

g-f7256f288c.how: Both results describe the same outcome: the corrected iron-reduction marker removes the shallow-over-deep clay pattern and no cohort comparison differs. Only the Bacillota_B project states the 50% and 11% original rates and the 40% and 56% corrected rates.

lanes.bacillota_b_subsurface_accessory--9886d5: Shallow, deep and soil iron-reduction rates after correction
lanes.clay_confined_subsurface--7edbee75: Clay cohort iron-reduction comparisons after marker correction

g-f7256f288c.question: Does the corrected iron-reduction marker still show more reducers in shallow clay?
g-f7256f288c.sentence: Both projects report that after correcting the iron-reduction marker, the earlier excess of iron reducers in shallow over deep clay disappeared. One gives original rates of 50% shallow and 11% deep.
g-f7256f288c.title: Corrected iron-reduction detector removes shallow-over-deep clay pattern in both projects
